title: China chip exports jump 136% to US$45b as AI frenzy jacks up prices
source_used: Sri Lanka Guardian (same customs data as SCMP headline)
key_facts: China's integrated-circuit exports rose 136% year on year to US$45 billion in September, per customs data released Wednesday 14 Oct 2026.
The number of chips shipped rose only 1%, to 32.7 billion units, so the rise reflects higher prices.
Over the first nine months, exports were 275.2 billion units worth nearly US$302 billion; value growth was 108%.
Total exports rose 36.3% to US$447.18 billion in September.
Customs vice-minister Wang Jun linked growth to worldwide AI computing investment.
Memory imports rose 150% in nine months and chip imports 56.6%.
quote_evidence: China’s integrated circuit exports surged 136 per cent year on year to US$45 billion in September, outpacing the 108 per cent growth recorded during the first nine months of the year as demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure contributed to higher chip prices.
The value of exports rose sharply even though the volume of shipments increased by only 1 per cent, to 32.7 billion integrated circuit units, according to customs data released on Wednesday.
why_it_matters_hint: Chip prices, not volumes, are driving the jump, so AI demand is making memory chips dearer worldwide.
notes: SCMP page blocked (403); text read from Sri Lanka Guardian, which does not name SCMP; headline figures match. Official customs data.
